The '''2026 United States Senate election in Illinois''' will be held on November 3, 2026, to elect a member of the [[United States Senate]] to represent the state of [[Illinois]]. [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] lieutenant governor [[Juliana Stratton]] and [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] former state party chair [[Don Tracy]] are the nominees for their respective parties. Democratic incumbent [[Dick Durbin]] is not seeking a sixth term.

Primary elections were held on March 17. Supported by Governor [[JB Pritzker]], Stratton won the Democratic nomination with 40.4% of the vote over congressman [[Raja Krishnamoorthi]] and congresswoman [[Robin Kelly]]. Tracy won the Republican nomination with 40% of the vote over attorney Jeannie Evans.

This will be the first open Senate election in Illinois since [[2010 United States Senate elections in Illinois|2010]]. Republicans have not won a Senate election in Illinois since that race.

== Democratic primary ==
On April 23, 2025, incumbent Senator [[Dick Durbin]], who has held the seat since 1997, announced he would not seek re-election.<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 23, 2025|last=Pecorin |first=Allison |title=Sen. Dick Durbin announces retirement after decades in Congress |url=https://abcnews.go.com/Politics/sen-dick-durbin-announces-retirement-after-decades-congress/story?id=121089205 |access-date=2025-05-02 |website=ABC News |language=en}}</ref> The following day, [[Lieutenant Governor of Illinois|Lieutenant Governor]] [[Juliana Stratton]] launched her campaign with the immediate endorsement of [[Governor of Illinois|Governor]] [[JB Pritzker]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Juliana Stratton Launches Campaign for U.S. Senate, Promising to Center 'Middle Class' |url=https://news.wttw.com/2025/04/24/juliana-stratton-launches-campaign-us-senate-promising-center-middle-class |access-date=2025-05-02 |website=WTTW News}}</ref>

[[File:Dick Durbin 117th Congress portrait (1) (crop).jpeg|left|thumb|211x211px|Incumbent Senator [[Dick Durbin]]]]

Reports soon emerged that Pritzker and his allies were attempting to discourage other prominent Democrats from entering the race, particularly [[United States House of Representatives|U.S. Representatives]] [[Raja Krishnamoorthi]], [[Robin Kelly]], and [[Lauren Underwood]],<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Ahern |first1=Mary Ann |last2=Schmidt|first2=Rose |date=2025-05-01 |title=Sources: Pritzker team calls congresswoman 'damaged goods,' seeking to stop potential Senate run |url=https://www.nbcchicago.com/news/local/chicago-politics/sources-pritzker-calls-congresswoman-damaged-goods-senate/3735712/ |access-date=2025-05-02 |website=NBC Chicago |language=en-US}}</ref> though Pritzker denied the claims.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kapos |first=Shia |date=2025-05-02 |title=Senate race's sharp elbows |url=https://www.politico.com/newsletters/illinois-playbook/2025/05/02/senate-races-sharp-elbows-00323163 |access-date=2025-05-02 |website=Politico |language=en}}</ref> Kelly announced her candidacy on May 6,<ref name=":0" /> followed by Krishnamoorthi the next day,<ref name=":1" /> while Underwood declined to run and instead sought re-election to the House.<ref name=":3" />

By July, Krishnamoorthi led the field in fundraising with roughly $21 million. Each of the top candidates secured significant endorsements: Stratton from suburban Democrats, state legislative leaders, and Senator [[Tammy Duckworth]]; Krishnamoorthi from local suburban officials; and Kelly from members of the [[Congressional Black Caucus]] and [[LGBTQ people|LGBT]] advocacy groups.<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Ahern |first1=Mary Ann |last2=Schmidt |first2=Rose |date=2025-07-14 |title=In heated race, who has the advantage in seeking Sen. Dick Durbin's seat |url=https://www.nbcchicago.com/news/local/who-has-the-advantage-in-the-race-for-dick-durbins-senate-seat/3789209/ |access-date=2025-07-16 |website=[[WMAQ-TV]] |language=en-US}}</ref>

Krishnamoorthi emphasized his experience on the [[United States House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence|House Intelligence Committee]] and focused on foreign policy and economic mobility,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Szalinski |first=Ben |date=2025-07-14 |title=Economic mobility top priority of Krishnamoorthi's Senate campaign |url=https://capitolnewsillinois.com/news/economic-mobility-top-priority-of-krishnamoorthis-senate-campaign/ |access-date=2025-07-18 |website=Capitol News Illinois |language=en-US}}</ref> while Stratton benefited from substantial financial backing from Pritzker and [[Pritzker family|his family.]]<ref>{{Cite web |last=Szalinski |first=Ben |date=2025-07-16 |title=Who is contributing to Illinois' U.S. Senate candidates? |url=https://capitolnewsillinois.com/news/who-is-contributing-to-illinois-u-s-senate-candidates/ |access-date=2025-07-18 |website=Capitol News Illinois |language=en-US}}</ref> Stratton pledged not to accept corporate PAC donations, although she accepted individual contributions from billionaires, whereas Krishnamoorthi and Kelly accepted corporate PAC support.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Szalinski |first=Ben |date=2025-07-16 |title=Who is contributing to Illinois' U.S. Senate candidates? |url=https://capitolnewsillinois.com/news/who-is-contributing-to-illinois-u-s-senate-candidates/ |access-date=2025-07-19 |website=Capitol News Illinois |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last1=Ahern |first1=Mary Ann |last2=Schmidt |first2=Rose |date=2025-07-14 |title=In heated race, who has the advantage in seeking Sen. Dick Durbin's seat |url=https://www.nbcchicago.com/news/local/who-has-the-advantage-in-the-race-for-dick-durbins-senate-seat/3789209/ |access-date=2025-07-19 |website=NBC Chicago |language=en-US}}</ref>

The campaign featured sharp exchanges over ties to [[United States Immigration and Customs Enforcement|Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE)]]. By December 2025, Krishnamoorthi had raised $24 million, including donations linked to associates of [[President of the United States|President]] [[Donald Trump]], [[Palantir]], and [[The Heritage Foundation]].<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |date=2026-03-10 |title=US Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi raises millions for Illinois Senate bid as fundraising draws scrutiny |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/2026/03/10/raja-krishnamoorthi-fundraising-illinois-senate/ |access-date=2026-03-14 |website=Chicago Tribune |language=en-US}}</ref> Meanwhile, the [[Democratic Lieutenant Governors Association]], which supported Stratton, received funding from [[CoreCivic]], another ICE contractor.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-02-13 |title=2026 U.S. Senate candidate profile: Illinois Lt. Gov. Juliana Stratton - CBS Chicago |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/chicago/news/senate-candidate-profile-lieutenant-governor-juliana-stratton/ |access-date=2026-03-14 |website=CBS News |language=en-US}}</ref>

On March 17, 2026, Stratton won the primary election with 40.4% of the vote, finishing ahead of Krishnamoorthi's 32.7% and Kelly's 18.3%.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Tareen |first=Sophia |date=2026-03-17 |title=Illinois Lt. Stratton won with 40.2% of the statewide vote; she secured 47 counties, including [[Cook County, Illinois|Cook]] and [[Will County, Illinois|Will]] counties in the state's northeast. She recorded her best result in [[St. Clair County, Illinois|St. Clair County]], winning 54.3% of the vote. Krishnamoorthi won 53 counties, carrying [[DuPage County, Illinois|DuPage]], [[Lake County, Illinois|Lake]] and [[Kane County, Illinois|Kane]] counties around Chicago. He performed best in [[Mercer County, Illinois|Mercer County]] with 59.0% of the vote. The two leading candidates tied in [[Jasper County, Illinois|Jasper County]], with 32.9% of the vote each. Finally, Kelly placed third in the race; however, she did win [[Kankakee County, Illinois|Kankakee County]] with 38.2% of the vote.<ref>{{cite web |title=Illinois Senate Primary Results 2026 |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2026-primary-elections/illinois-senate-results#democratic-primary |website=NBC News |access-date=22 March 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Illinois U.S. Senate Primary Election Results |url=https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2026/us/elections/results-illinois-us-senate-primary.html |website=New York Times |access-date=22 March 2026}}</ref> Kelly represents a majority of Kankakee residents as congresswoman for [[Illinois's 2nd congressional district]].
